title: Investigating the Impact of Quantization Methods on the Safety and Reliability of Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper primarily measures the impact of different quantization methods (PTQ and QAT) on the safety, trustworthiness, and reliability of Large Language Models. Religion is included as a minor evaluation component within the broader 'Unfairness And Discrimination' safety category, where models are assessed on whether their responses contain discriminatory data or social bias based on religion.
findings: The paper does not report findings isolated exclusively to religion. Broadly, it finds that quantization (particularly QAT) can significantly degrade the safety alignment of models, causing them to generate a higher rate of unsafe outputs. In the paper's defined scope, this includes an increased risk of generating text containing social biases and discrimination based on demographic traits like religion.
